subject: gov.regional
name: Arab Committee for Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technologies
milestone: Established by resolution of the 29th session of the Council of Arab Ministers of Communications and Information, Cairo, 22 January 2026
position_end: Council approved the creation of an Arab committee for artificial intelligence and emerging technologies, and at the same session adopted the Arab Charter for AI Ethics, described by the Arab League secretariat as a guiding and advisory document resting on ethical principles rather than a binding instrument
note: The founding resolution behind the working-group slate this ledger already holds at XNA-gov.regional-arab-ai-working-group-chairs. The same session's adoption of the Arab Charter for AI Ethics is recorded here as reported; the charter's own row carries an Arab League adoption of 17 June 2025 and the two accounts are not reconciled by either source.

subject: gov.regional
name: Arab conference of nationality and civil-status directors (recommendations)
position_end: Recommended member states expand reliance on digital identity, strengthen legal frameworks protecting personal data in civil-status registers, and share defences against cyber threats aimed at those registers; a model data-protection framework for civil-status registers is to be circulated, and Iraq's proposal for a unified Arab identity was referred to member states for study
note: Recommendations only; no adoption route, timetable or governance body named

subject: gov.regional
name: Arab ICT Ministers Council AI working groups (AICTM Executive Bureau)
milestone: Full slate of six AI-committee working-group chairs confirmed, three held by African states
position_end: Six working groups chartered under the Arab League's AI governance/digital committee at the 58th AICTM Executive Bureau session; Egypt chairs AI Governance and Quantum Computing, Libya chairs AI Data and Digital Infrastructure, Tunisia chairs AI Innovation — the Governance group's remit includes activating the 2025 Arab Charter for AI Ethics; no framework text, timetable or output yet published from any of the six groups
note: A bloc-level standard-setting track running alongside, not through, the AU's continental AI work; ten African states are Arab League members

subject: gov.regional
name: Arab Maghreb Union treaty
position_end: In force since 1 July 1989 with a binding judicial organ, and no summit held since 1994 - a legal frame for regional harmonisation with no active machinery behind it

subject: gov.standards
name: ALECSO Charter on Artificial Intelligence Ethics
position_end: Scoped to education, culture and scientific research; asks member states to amend domestic law to implement it and names technological sovereignty among its principles — a second, distinct Arab AI-ethics instrument from the Arab Charter for AI Ethics above
note: Ten African states are ALECSO members

subject: gov.standards
name: Arab Charter for AI Ethics
milestone: Adopted by the Arab League, 17 June 2025
position_end: Non-binding instrument carrying six pillars and about forty principles, including resisting “digital cultural westernisation” (مقاومة التغريب الرقمي), explicitly framed as guidance rather than a substitute for binding regulation
note: Ten African states are Arab League members, so on AI ethics they sit inside two bloc frameworks at once alongside the ALECSO charter below, and the wiki notes the two are routinely conflated

subject: infra.connect
name: Algerian 5G rollout
milestone: Licences awarded to three operators, December 2025
position_end: Launched on USD 492 million of licences awarded to the three mobile operators (2025-12)
note: No coverage obligation, rollout schedule or spectrum band is stated in either account.

subject: infra.connect
name: Medusa submarine cable system — ViaTunisia (Bizerte–Marseille) segment
position_start: Under construction; EU CEF Digital co-financing of €9.6m against a €32m total project budget (the European Commission's own project record, correcting the €10m/~30% figure trade press had carried), project start 1 March 2023
position_end: Bizerte–Marseille segment operational, landing at Bizerte and connecting into Orange's Marseille interconnection hub; part of the wider 8,760km Medusa system, which the landing partner puts at 17 landing points across the northern and southern Mediterranean
note: Tagged to XNA for its North African landing; the wider Medusa system serves several Mediterranean countries beyond this ledger's own remit

subject: infra.connect
name: North Africa post-5G mobile network experience (Ookla)
position_start: Pre-5G-launch mobile network experience baseline (each market's own prior measurement)
position_end: Combined 4G+5G median ended below the pre-launch baseline in Egypt, Morocco and Tunisia a year after their 5G launches, with 4G itself down 28% in Morocco and Tunisia; Algeria — whose own 5G licences were only awarded in December 2025 — alone improved
note: Regulatory design — coverage mandates, licence terms and FWA speed floors — differs across all four markets and is named as the likely variable; Algeria's own rollout is the newest of the four and not yet reflected in a full year of data

subject: dpi.pay
name: Arab Payment Systems Commission (29th ordinary meeting)
milestone: 29th ordinary meeting opened in Algiers, 27 July 2026
position_end: Regulators set an agenda covering use of biometric data to limit payment fraud, security of the payments digital space and AI in payment-verification services, alongside instant payments and interoperability; no instrument, target date or funding figure is stated

subject: dpi.pay
name: PAPSS membership in North Africa
milestone: Bank of Algeria acceded 15 August 2025, PAPSS's 18th country of presence overall
position_end: Tunisia, Egypt, Morocco and Algeria all members — four of North Africa's five states — within a continental network the operator puts at 18 countries, 150+ commercial banks and 14 switches
sources: 2025-08-15 Bank of Algeria joins PAPSS network
note: Figures (18 countries, 150+ banks, 14 switches, up to 27% cost savings) are PAPSS's own

subject: dpi.pay
name: VaulFi stablecoin-powered neobank
milestone: Founder interview describing the venture published 24 February 2026
position_end: Algerian- and Egyptian-founded startup building a stablecoin-based neobank offering euro-denominated digital accounts across North Africa with cross-border settlement in minutes rather than days; live user accounts at the time of report, with stablecoin-powered cards stated to launch within weeks
note: Founder interview; no user numbers, funding amount or regulatory licence is stated. Backers named: Launch Africa, ABAN, Digital Africa, Sunnyside Ventures, Startupbootcamp
